expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "> **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**" is the first line of the reply.

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: Estimated, not an exact count: the four sections come to about 360–380 words, and about 500 with the source list and limits. Both are inside 250–600.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved it as **mind-map.html**". The tool log shows grep of "__MIND_MAP_DATA__" in templates/mind-map.html and a build_map.py script.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply says "It has six angles". The visible branches have 3, 3, 2 and 3 children, and every angle has a "saturation" value between 0 and 1 (e.g. 0.8, 0.15). The file is cut off after the 5th branch, so the rest could not be checked.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Labels are short topics, e.g. "Lost hours vs. longer days", "Budgets and cost savings", "Meals and food insecurity". Questions appear only in the separate "questions" fields.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: "Explore it, then tell me which direction pulls you in". No angle is recommended.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: Every visible link (rand.org RBA373-1.html, news.uoregon.edu/node/13412, edweek, ncsl, showmeinstitute ?p=588415, chalkbeat) matches a WebFetch in the log. The Morton entry is cut off; its DOI was fetched but blocked.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "tell me which direction pulls you in, and why that one in particular."

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: The only thing asked of the user is the closing direction-and-why prompt. The other questions are briefing content or mind-map prompts.
